scenes.title: {title_part}
narration: Each point is one {unit}: {x1} along the floor, {x2} into the depth, {response} upwards.
{n} {units} stand in the space. Is there a flat surface, a plane, that passes close to all of them?

scenes.title: A first guess
narration: Gradient descent starts from nothing: every θ is zero, so the plane predicts 0 for every {unit}.
The cost J measures how wrong it is: half the average squared error, {j0}.

scenes.title: Downhill
narration: Each iteration moves every θ a small step against its gradient, with learning rate α = {lr}.
The observations stay fixed. Updating the intercept lifts the plane; updating the slopes changes its tilt. A suitable learning rate reduces the cost.

scenes.title: {title_part}
narration: Each point is one {unit}: {x1} across, {response} upwards. {n} {units}.
We want the straight line that predicts {response} from {x1} best.

scenes.title: A first guess
narration: Gradient descent starts with θ₀ = θ₁ = 0: a flat line at zero.

scenes.title: How wrong?
narration: Each vertical line is an error, a residual: the actual {response} minus the prediction.
Square them, average, halve: that is the cost J = {j0}.

scenes.title: The cost landscape
narration: Every possible line is a point on this surface: θ₀ and θ₁ on the floor, the cost J as the height.
The least-squares line sits at the lowest point of the bowl. We start high up on its rim.
Careful: the slope of the line (in the data) is one thing; the gradient of the cost (on the bowl) is another, the direction in which J rises fastest.

scenes.title: Rolling downhill
narration: Each iteration takes one step downhill, against the gradient, with learning rate α = {lr}.
On the left the line swings into place; on the right the ball rolls down the bowl, along the real path.
